title: Gabriele Orrico — 'A mission can survive its founder and still fail the people it exists to serve'
summary: Orrico works on operating models and governance and is part of the Incorruptible community. His post takes the book's structural protections as settled and asks what comes after: once a mission is locked, who decides what it means. Founder intent and a successor's reading can diverge from what employees experience, and he treats that gap as a governance problem of its own. The post carries 21 likes and an 8-comment thread.
blockquote: A mission can survive its founder and still fail the people it exists to serve. … Who gets to challenge the interpretation without being accused of disloyalty? Because whoever controls what the mission means has considerable power over whom it serves.
